title: Microburst Absorption Layer for NCCL Overlap and Kernel Handoffs
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
We observe periodic short-lived throughput collapses ("microbursts") in mixed-length workloads running multi-GPU prefill+decode paths. These microbursts manifest as transient NCCL congestion spikes combined with suboptimal attention kernel choices that force expensive memory copies and stall token handoffs between tensor/pipeline stages. Impact: tail latency regressions (~2x) for a small fraction of requests, higher token cost due to repeated kernel fallback and re-allocation, and occasional SLA alerts for P99 latency on heavy workloads.

Goals:
- Reduce the frequency and severity of microbursts by absorbing short correlated token spikes at the runtime layer without increasing steady-state latency.
- Improve kernel handoff stability during transient congestion so KV cache reuse and attention-specialized kernels remain effective.
- Maintain fairness across tenants and avoid prolonged deprioritization.

Design proposal (high-level):
1) Microburst Detector (lightweight): continuous estimator that tracks per-GPU and cross-GPU token ingress rates, short-window variance (10-200ms), and NCCL queue depth proxies. Emits a graded signal (0-1) representing microburst intensity. Implemented as a C++ shim in the rendezvous layer with a fast eBPF-like sampling loop for Linux hosts.

2) Absorption Buffer (token holding window): a small bounded token buffer per request stream that can temporarily absorb 1-4 tokens when the microburst signal exceeds a threshold. Buffering is latency-aware: it only applies to requests with flexible latency SLAs (configurable per-route) and will be bypassed for low-latency-critical routes.

3) Kernel Hint Generator: when a buffer is used, emit kernel hints to downstream stages that prefer attention-kernels which are robust under intermittent comm contention (e.g., memory-local fused attention vs. split-kernel attention) and avoid immediate memory reallocation calls. Hints are soft; runtime can still pick optimized kernels when safe.

4) NCCL Overlap Coordinator extension: integrate the microburst signal into the NCCL scheduling heuristics so small allreduce/allgather windows can be deferred by a few ms to increase overlap with compute, smoothing traffic and avoiding bursts that block prefill-to-decode handoffs.

5) Backpressure policy and fairness: if bursts persist beyond a configured window, switch to explicit backpressure mode and shed low-priority requests (or route them to lower-cost dedicated pools).

Instrumentation / Metrics:
- microburst_score (per-GPU, per-request): rolling 10/50/200ms quantiles
- absorption_rate: fraction of requests that used the buffer
- kernel_switch_rate: how often hints caused kernel changes
- NCCL short-window tail latency distribution (1ms buckets)
- P50/P95/P99 token latency and tokens-per-second during detected bursts
- cost_delta (tokens rerun / kernel fallback extra cost)

Telemetry & dashboards: create a new "microburst" panel in runtime-ops Grafana linking NCCL metrics, kernel selection traces, and request timelines. Add an endpoint-level rollout KPI for latency impact.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (dev): implement detector + simulator that replays production traces to validate heuristics. Unit tests against synthetic burst patterns.
- Phase 2 (canary): enable in a small fleet behind a feature flag for non-critical routes (internal test tenants). Collect telemetry and run AB tests vs baseline.
- Phase 3 (opt-in): expose route-level knob in Console to enable absorption for customers.
- Phase 4 (auto): if signals prove stable, enable adaptive mode for all eligible hosted requests with a fallback to previous behavior on regressions.

Testing strategy:
- Replay historical traffic containing known microbursts in our workload replay tool; assert P99 improvements and no worsening of P50.
- Hardware-in-loop tests with synthetic NCCL traffic generators to validate overlap coordination under heterogeneous bandwidth.
- End-to-end integration tests for KV cache correctness during buffered handoffs.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Buffering could increase tail latency for latency-sensitive customers. Mitigation: per-route opt-out and strict upper bound on buffer-induced delay.
- Risk: Kernel hint instability might cause oscillation between kernels. Mitigation: hysteresis windows and minimum kernel hold times.
- Risk: NCCL scheduling changes could interact badly with provider drivers. Mitigation: test matrix across NVIDIA driver versions and a rollback feature flag.

Success criteria:
- 30-60% reduction in microburst-induced P99 tail spikes on canary population within 2 weeks of rollout.
- No regression in P50 latency beyond 5% on any route.
- Reduced kernel fallback rate by at least 20% during detected bursts.

Artifacts & links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Microburst+Absorption+Layer (draft)
- Perf replay trace set: gs://redwood-perf/traces/microburst-2026-02
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6124
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/runtime/microburst-panel

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Sampling granularity tradeoff: 10ms vs 50ms windows for the detector (latency of detection vs noise).
- Acceptable default buffer size per-route (1 vs 4 tokens) and how to express as Console policy.
- Interaction model with Dedicated capacity where tenants expect strict throughput guarantees.

Next steps (short term):
- Assign prototype owner for detector shim (Ravi) and simulation lead (Leah Kim).
- Implement simulator and run across three representative traces by 2026-03-05.
